messages:
sre-bot: ALERT: Detected elevated TLS handshake failures 09:12 UTC — aggregation shows spikes from egress POPs in us-west2 and eu-central1. Automatic reroute attempted and partially failed.

maria (oncall): paging chart looks nasty, customers in those regions seeing 502/523. I'm attaching pcap summary to the incident ticket. Starting mitigation runbook.

jay (netops): seeing BGP withdrawals to two transit peers from the eu-central1 POP. Peers are flapping prefixes to our egress ASN. Temporary workaround: shift egress to alt-peering via pop-eu-alt and pop-us-alt.

deepa (eng-runtime): can we toggle smart-routing policy to force region->alt-pop for affected regions? If we switch to policy 'egress-alt-first' we should avoid the flaky peer.

maria (oncall): doing it now. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing update --policy egress-alt-first --scope eu-central1,us-west2
```
Applying... will monitor.

sre-bot: ACTIONED: routing policy update submitted by maria. Rollout id: roll_2212345678_1. Watch for metric delta in 2 minutes.

mike (support): drafting a short customer notification. Suggest: "We are aware of an issue impacting API requests from EU and US West customers; we are mitigating by rerouting traffic and expect reduced errors shortly. If you see continued errors, reply with your request-id." Any changes?

lucas (product-ops): please include affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Also link to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2212345678

maria (oncall): routing change reduced 5xx by ~60% in us-west2, eu-central1 still 30% above baseline. Jay, can we bring up extra pop-egress-cache in eu to short-circuit some long tail errors? Cache will keep idempotent generation responses.

jay (netops): provisioning pop-egress-cache-eu now. ETA ~6m.

deepa (eng-runtime): temporary config to enable cached fallback for short requests (<512 tokens):
```
runtime.config.set({"cache_fallback": true, "max_tokens":512})
```
Already enabling for eu-central1.

sre-bot: METRIC UPDATE: 09:28 UTC — total 5xx down to 20% above baseline. Continuing to monitor.

mike (support): customer notification draft v1 pasted below — please sign off.
---
Hi — we're investigating an issue affecting API requests originating from EU (eu-central1) and US West (us-west2). Some requests may receive transient errors or higher latency. Our engineers have rerouted traffic to alternative egress nodes and enabled temporary cache fallbacks. We're monitoring and will update you by 09:45 UTC or when we have more info. If you're actively impacted and need help, reply with a sample request-id and region.
---

lucas (product-ops): looks good, add "No action required on your side" and a link to status page.

mike (support): updated and posted to status page. Status page entry:
- Summary: Regional egress interruptions causing elevated errors in EU and US West
- Impact: API requests may fail or have elevated latency for customers routed through those regions
- Mitigation: Traffic rerouted to alternate egress POPs; cache fallback enabled for short requests; team working with transit peers

sre-bot: STATUSPAGE PUBLISHED: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2212345678 (investigating)

deepa (eng-runtime): still seeing occasional TLS handshake timeouts from upstream in eu-central1. Working with transit provider rep (cc @jay) — they see a partial hardware issue on one edge router.

jay (netops): provider confirmed flaky module, will replace. ETA 45m. Our reroute keeps traffic away but long tail will persist until replacement.

maria (oncall): doc for handoff to night oncall (sre-night):
- Current state: traffic rerouted; 5xx reduced to ~10% above baseline; cache fallback active in eu and us-west
- Open actions: monitor roll_2212345678_1, ensure pop-egress-cache-eu comes online, follow provider's replacement update
- Escalations: if 5xx >30% for >10m, escalate to netops lead and CCO
- Contact list: jay, deepa, lucas, mike

sre-night (oncall-night): copying, I'm taking handoff at 10:00 PDT. Will watch for regression and update status page every 30m.

maria (oncall): thanks — adding final note for postmortem: track decision to use cache fallback and measure correctness impact on model outputs. also log all request-ids we substituted via cache.

sre-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: handoff recorded. Thread locked for updates to incident channel only. Use thread for comms.

mike (support): customer reply received from a major customer in eu-central1 with sample request-id req_9f3b2. Forwarded to deepa for trace.

deepa (eng-runtime): traced req_9f3b2 — TLS timeout at the provider hop before our cache. Customer response suggests small latency spike before failure; will include in postmortem.

sre-night (oncall-night): acknowledged. pushing scheduled check at 10:30 PDT and will update status page.

maria (oncall): closing active remediation: roll_id roll_2212345678_1 stable. Leaving incident in 'monitoring' state until provider completes hardware replacement.

sre-bot: INCIDENT MONITORING: last update 09:40 UTC. Metrics show gradual normalization. Next scheduled update at 10:30 PDT.
